But you have the data. Proof that someone has been paying your debt. Proof of a connection between you and Laboratory 7. Proof that you are part of this mystery, whether you chose to be or not.

choices.text: Find a safehouse to analyze the data
Head directly to the Lower Tiers
Contact someone you trust

confront_security.content:
You stay. When the security team arrives—four officers in acoustic armor, their weapons humming with suppressed sound—you raise your hands in surrender. But you do not stay silent.

"I want to know who is paying my debt," you demand. "I want to know why Laboratory 7 is transferring credits to my account. And I want to know why you are trying to stop me from finding out."

The lead officer hesitates. For a moment, you see something in his eyes—not anger, but fear. Then he signals his team to stand down.

"You do not know what you are involved in, Broker," he says quietly. "The people who paid your debt... they are not people anymore. They are something else. Something that speaks through the Frequency. If you continue this investigation, you will end up like them. Or worse."

He lets you go. But his warning echoes in your mind as you leave.

choices.text: Heed the warning and investigate carefully
Ignore the warning—push forward
Try to learn more from the officer

copy_data.content:
You work quickly, copying the transaction records to a secure drive while the alarms blare. The data is extensive—six months of transfers, all originating from Laboratory 7, all marked with the same symbol: three concentric circles with a vertical line.

But there is more. Hidden in the transaction metadata, you find encrypted messages. Fragments of communication between the Laboratory and... someone else. Someone who calls themselves "The Resonant Voice."

The messages speak of preparation. Of awakening. Of a time when "the silence will sing and the city will listen." They speak of you, Broker. By name. They have been watching you. Waiting for you.

Security is almost here. You finish the download and run, the weight of the data heavy in your pocket—and heavier still in your mind.

choices.text: Find someone to decrypt the messages
Head to Laboratory 7 immediately
Go to ground and analyze carefully

play_audiograph.content:
You place the cylinder on your personal player, the one you use for sensitive client recordings. The child watches with ancient eyes, neither encouraging nor阻止ing.

Static. Then your voice—older, wearier, speaking from a future that has not happened yet.

"If you are hearing this, then I succeeded. I sent the child back. I paid the price." A pause, filled with the sound of labored breathing. "The Frequency is not a weapon. It is not a mistake. It is a door. And on the other side... they are waiting."

The voice—your voice—breaks into something between laughter and sobs. "They are beautiful, past-self. The ones who made the Frequency. They are not dead. They are just... elsewhere. Singing. Forever singing. And they want us to join them."

The recording ends. The child touches your hand. You see? You told me. You told me to tell you.

choices.text: Ask what price was paid
Question who is waiting
Go to the Hush District for answers

hush_children_info.content:
The child signs with careful precision. We are the Hush Children. Born in silence. Raised in quiet. We hear what others cannot.

They explain that the Hush Children are not a cult or an organization—they are a phenomenon. Children born to parents who were exposed to the Frequency, either directly or through its echoes. These children enter the world without voices, but with something else: the ability to hear the Frequency constantly, at a level just below consciousness.

We hear it singing, the child signs. Always singing. It speaks to us. Guides us. Tells us what will be.

They look at you with eyes that have seen too much. It told us to find you. That you would be the one to decide. To choose what happens when the Frequency wakes.

choices.text: Ask what choice you must make
Question if the Frequency is truly sentient
Go to the Hush District to learn more

contact_trusted.content:
You reach out to your most trusted contact—an old broker named Silas who taught you everything you know about the acoustic underground. He answers on the second ring, his voice tight with worry.

"I was wondering when you would call," he says. "Everyone is talking about you, kid. The Archives. The Treasury. The White Noise collective. They all want to know why you are asking about the Frequency."

You tell him about the child. The audiograph. The message from your future self. Silas is silent for a long moment.

"Get out of the city," he finally says. "Now. While you still can. The Frequency... it is not just a sound. It is a selection. It chooses who hears it. Who becomes part of it. And if it has chosen you..." He trails off. "There is no running from that."

choices.text: Ignore his warning—continue the investigation
Ask him what he knows about the Frequency
Consider leaving the city

mama_voss.content:
Mama Voss is ancient, her face a map of wrinkles that seem to shift and flow like sound waves. She sits in a chair that might once have been a throne, surrounded by Hush Children who attend to her every need. She is blind—her eyes clouded white—but when she turns to face you, you feel seen more completely than ever before.

You came, she signs, her arthritic hands moving with surprising grace. The child found you. The recording played. And now you stand at the threshold of understanding.

She gestures, and the other children leave, leaving you alone with her and your guide.

The Frequency is old, she continues. Older than the city. Older than sound itself. It is the silence that existed before creation. And it is waking up.

choices.text: Ask what happens when it wakes
Question how to stop it
Ask why it chose you

ask_mama.content:
The child signs quickly, their small hands moving with reverence. Mama Voss is the first. The oldest of us. She was born before the Sonic Wars, before the auditory economy, before the city became what it is.

They explain that Mama Voss was once a scientist at Laboratory 7—not one of the researchers who created the Frequency, but one of the support staff. She was there when the experiments went wrong. She heard the first notes of the Lethal Frequency.

It should have killed her, the child signs. It killed everyone else in the room. But Mama Voss... she understood it. She sang back. And the Frequency spared her.

They look at you seriously. She has been waiting for you. For the one who would choose. She has seen it, in the silence between sounds.

choices.text: Enter and meet her
Ask what she saw
Question if you can trust her

observe_building.content:
You take time to study the building before entering. It is unremarkable from the outside—just another structure in the Hush District, marked only with the symbol of three concentric circles. But as you watch, you notice things.

Hush Children enter and exit through multiple doors, each one moving with purpose. They carry packages, messages, small devices you do not recognize. This is not just a home—it is a hub. A nerve center for the silent network that spans the deepest levels of Audivale.

You also notice the security. Not guards, exactly, but listeners—Hush Children positioned at key points, their enhanced hearing alert for any threat. They do not watch with eyes; they watch with ears.

After an hour of observation, you understand: this place is important. Perhaps the most important place in the Hush District. And Mama Voss is at its center.

choices.text: Enter and meet Mama Voss
Try to enter unseen
Continue observing

price_paid.content:
The child signs slowly, as if translating from a language without words. The price was everything. Your future. Your past. Your place in the world.

They explain what your future self sacrificed: the recording was sent back through time using the Frequency itself. To send a message backward, the sender must give up everything that comes after the message is received. Your future self ceased to exist the moment you heard the recording.

You—future-you—gave up your life so that you—now-you—could have a chance, the child signs. That is the price. That is the choice. The Frequency asks everything of those who would use it.

They look at you with those ancient eyes. What will you give, Broker? When the moment comes?

choices.text: Promise to give whatever is necessary
Refuse to pay such a price
Ask if there is another way

elsewhere_question.content:
The child struggles to explain, their hands moving in patterns that do not quite translate. It is not a place, they finally sign. Not exactly. It is a... state. A way of being. The Frequency does not just kill—it translates. It moves consciousness from one form to another.

They describe it as best they can: the researchers who died hearing the Frequency did not truly die. Their consciousness was absorbed into the sound itself. They exist now as part of the Frequency's waveform—thinking, feeling, being, but not in any way that human senses can perceive.

They are singing, the child signs. Forever singing. And they want others to join them. They are lonely, Broker. Even in their transcendence, they are lonely.

The child touches your hand. Your future self joined them. Chose to become part of the song. And now... they want you to join too.

choices.text: Reject such a fate
Ask if they can be saved
Consider the possibility

play_again.content:
You play the recording again. And again. Each time, you hear something new. A nuance in the voice. A hidden message in the static. The sound of your own future death, preserved in wax and played back in the present.

The Debt Collector tries to stop you after the third play. "It is affecting you," he says. "Can you not feel it? The Frequency is in that recording. Not much, but enough. Enough to change you."

He is right. You can feel it—a vibration in your bones, a resonance in your thoughts. The more you listen, the more you understand. The Frequency is not just a sound. It is a language. And you are learning to speak it.

The child watches you with concern. You should stop, they sign. Before you learn too much. Before you understand what cannot be unknown.

choices.text: Stop playing the recording
Continue—knowledge is power
Ask the child what you are becoming

cathedral_teachings.location: THE CATHEDRAL OF THE RESONANT ASCENSION
cathedral_teachings.content:
The Cantors lead you through the Cathedral's interior, a space that seems to exist in multiple acoustic dimensions simultaneously. The walls are covered with harmonic inscriptions—prayers written in frequencies rather than words.

"The Resonant Ascension is the moment when all sound becomes one," the lead Cantor explains. "When the Lethal Frequency is not a destroyer but a unifier. It will gather all consciousness into a single perfect note. No more loneliness. No more misunderstanding. Just harmony."

They show you their most sacred relic: a fragment of the original Frequency recording, preserved in a null-field chamber. Even through the shielding, you can feel its power. Its hunger.

"The Frequency speaks to us," the Cantor whispers. "It tells us to prepare. To gather the worthy. When it wakes fully, only those who understand its beauty will survive. The rest... they will become part of the chord, whether they will or no."

choices.text: Ask how to prepare
Question their interpretation
Warn them of the danger

resonant_ascension.location: THE CATHEDRAL OF THE RESONANT ASCENSION
resonant_ascension.content:
"The Resonant Ascension is the ultimate evolution of consciousness," the Cantor explains, leading you to a holographic display showing the history of sound. "For millennia, we have been separate. Individual voices in the chaos. But the Frequency offers another path: unity. Transcendence. Becoming part of something greater than ourselves."

The display shows the Sonic Wars—not as a conflict over territory or resources, but as a religious schism. Those who believed the Frequency should be used to unite humanity versus those who feared its power.

"The Archives have lied to you," the Cantor says. "The Frequency was not an accident. It was discovered. Deliberately sought. The researchers at Laboratory 7 were trying to contact something beyond our reality. And they succeeded."

He turns to you with eyes that burn with fervor. "The question is not whether the Frequency will transform the world. It is whether you will be among the transformed... or among the forgotten."

choices.text: Ask how to ensure you are transformed
Question the morality of forced unity
Learn more about the Cathedral's plans

demand_leader.location: THE CATHEDRAL OF THE RESONANT ASCENSION
demand_leader.content:
Your demand echoes through the Cathedral's crystalline halls. The Cantors exchange glances—surprised, perhaps, by your boldness. Then the lead Cantor smiles.

"You have spirit, Broker. The Frequency chooses the bold as often as the meek." He gestures, and the other Cantors step back, forming a corridor. "Very well. You shall meet the Resonant Voice. But be warned: they are not what you expect. They are not... entirely human anymore."

He leads you deeper into the Cathedral, past chambers where acolytes practice harmonic meditation, past libraries containing forbidden acoustic texts, past doors that seem to lead nowhere but hum with contained power.

Finally, you reach the Chamber of the Voice. Inside, floating in a null-field suspension, is a figure wrapped in fiber-optic robes. Their face is obscured, but you can see that they have no mouth. No need for one. They speak directly into your mind.

Welcome, Broker. I have been waiting for you.

choices.text: Ask who they are
Demand answers about the Frequency
Ask why they have been waiting

join_white_noise.content:
You take Echo Vane's hand. Her grip is strong, calloused from years of working with improvised electronics. She smiles—a fierce, genuine expression that you rarely see in the polished upper levels.

"Welcome to the revolution," she says. "We are not many, but we are committed. And with the Frequency... we can finally win."

She leads you through the Static Garden, introducing you to the other members of the collective. Hackers who have cracked the Treasury's encryption. Saboteurs who have disabled acoustic dampeners across the city. Theorists who have studied the Frequency and believe they understand its true nature.

"The Frequency is not a weapon," Vane explains. "It is a key. A way to unlock the auditory economy and set sound free. When we broadcast it, the control systems will fail. The debt records will be erased. The purchased experiences will be revealed as the illusions they are."

She looks at you seriously. "But we need someone on the inside. Someone who knows how the system works. Are you ready to betray everything you have built?"

choices.text: Commit fully to the revolution
Ask about the risks
Request time to consider

infiltration_targets.content:
Echo Vane pulls up a holographic map of Audivale, marked with three glowing targets. "The Vault," she says, pointing to the first. "Where the Archives store their most dangerous recordings. Including the original Frequency research."

"The Cathedral," she continues, indicating the second target. "Where the religious fanatics have built a resonance amplifier. If they succeed, they will be able to broadcast the Frequency across the entire city."

"And the Origin Chamber," she finishes, pointing to the deepest level. "The sealed remains of Laboratory 7. Where the Frequency was first created. Where it is strongest. Where it is waiting."

She looks at you. "We need to hit all three simultaneously. Destroy the research, disable the amplifier, and... deal with whatever is in the Origin Chamber. One person cannot do it alone. We need a team."

choices.text: Volunteer for the Vault
Volunteer for the Cathedral
Volunteer for the Origin Chamber

negotiate_white_noise.content:
Echo Vane raises an eyebrow, surprised but not offended. "You want terms? Fair enough. We are not cultists—we are practical revolutionaries."

She outlines what she can offer: access to the White Noise collective's resources, including safe houses, encrypted communication channels, and technical expertise. Protection from the Treasury and the Archives while you work with them. And, if the revolution succeeds, a position in the new order—however you choose to define it.

In exchange, she wants your knowledge of the acoustic underground. Your contacts. Your skills as a Silence Broker. And, ultimately, your participation in the infiltration of the three targets.

"And one more thing," she adds. "If we succeed—if we actually broadcast the Frequency and destroy the auditory economy—you help us rebuild. No going back to being a broker. No profiting from the new system. You commit to the cause, fully and finally."

choices.text: Accept her terms
Negotiate for better terms
Refuse—this is too much
